# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list spawns a burst of `wl` CLI processes on a fixed cadence — background `wl sync` every 60s plus a full refresh (`wl next`, 2× `wl list` mandatory subsets, expanded-children fetches) on every 30s auto-refresh tick — **regardless of whether the worklog database changed**. When the pane is idle (no agents writing, no remote activity), each cycle wastes 3–5 process spawns and a full git sync round-trip for zero visible change.

## Users

- **Herdr users running the selection list with auto-refresh/auto-sync on** — want the list to stay current without constant background `wl` process churn (spawn overhead, git fetch/pull/merge/push, lock contention with other panes).
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — the reduction in unnecessary `wl sync` invocations reduces lock-storm pressure between panes and cross-process DB churn.

Example user stories:
- As a Herdr user with an idle backlog, I want the selection list to avoid spawning any `wl` commands when nothing changed, so my machine isn't churning processes and git round-trips every 30–60s.
- As a Herdr user, I want background sync to still run at least once per configurable window (default 60s) even when nothing changed locally, so I still receive remote changes pushed by other machines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On an auto-refresh tick, when the worklog DB has not changed since the last refresh cycle, the pane spawns **zero** `wl` processes for that tick (no `wl next`, no `wl list`, no children fetches, no `wl sync`, no action-count fetch).
2. On an auto-sync tick, `wl sync` is skipped when (a) the DB has not changed since the last cycle **and** (b) the last successful sync is fresher than the configurable max-staleness cap (default 60s). If either condition fails, the sync runs (subject to the existing heartbeat / single-flight / `--if-idle` guards).
3. The max-staleness cap is configurable via the Herdr settings file (e.g. new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting, default `60000`), clamped to a sane minimum like the sync interval clamp.
4. Manual user actions — `S` (sync) and `r` (refresh) keypresses — always run, ignoring the gate.
5. The very first cycle after pane start always runs (no prior "last seen" signal), and any failure to read the DB-change signal fails **open** (the cycle runs), so the list can never go stale due to a signal-read error.
6. The existing cross-instance heartbeat (`last-sync-time`), single-flight, and `--if-idle` guards remain in place for syncs that do run.
7. Unit tests cover: gate skip/run decisions for refresh and sync ticks (changed/unchanged DB, stale/fresh last-sync, manual override, first-cycle, fail-open), plus the new setting's parse/clamp behavior.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin package (`packages/herdr`) has **zero npm dependencies** and intentionally duplicates small shared helpers per TUI (decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B) — a small pure helper duplicating the counter-read logic is consistent with this pattern.
- The DB-change signal must be cheap (a file read or two) and must NOT spawn a `wl` process itself — that is the whole point of the gate.
- The signal must be cross-process stable: the wl CLI read cache (F2) deliberately avoids SQLite file mtimes because "the SQLite files are rewritten by the app on every open/close cycle… file-based fingerprints are not stable across processes" (`src/read-cache.ts`). The gate must not produce false "changed" signals from the pane's own reads.
- Do not change wl CLI sync behavior itself; the incremental-sync work (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q) is separate scope.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` registers two scheduler tasks: `refresh` (every `refreshIntervalMs`, default 30s, always calls `doRefresh(false)` → spawns read commands) and `sync` (every `syncIntervalMs`, default 60s, calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`). Plus a `resume-poll` task that calls `doRefresh(true)` on hidden→visible transition.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` fire-and-forget with cross-instance heartbeat skip (`last-sync-time` marker, `isSyncHeartbeatFresh`), single-flight guard, and `--if-idle`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — all read commands (`wl next`, `wl list`, children, action-count) go through `runWl`; the CLI serves many from its on-disk read cache (F2), but a process spawn still occurs per command.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — the wl CLI maintains a monotonic per-worklog-dir **state counter** (`~/.cache/wl/state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`, `{ "state": N }`), bumped by every wl write command and by post-sync invalidation (`invalidateCacheForWrite`). This is the natural "DB changed" signal: cross-process, stable across reads, and already the CLI's freshness authority.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — typed settings JSON with clamped intervals; `syncIntervalMs` has a 60s minimum clamp.
- Manual `S`/`r` keypresses dispatch to `doSync()` / `doRefresh(true)` unconditionally.

## Desired change

- Add a small pure module in `packages/herdr` (e.g. `db-change.ts`) that:
  - resolves the wl cache dir (mirroring `resolveCacheDir()` precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wl` → `~/.cache/wl`);
  - reads the state counter for the resolved worklog dir (`state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`), returning the counter value (0 when absent); and
  - exposes a `DbChangeTracker`/helper that remembers the last-seen counter per pane and answers `dbChangedSinceLastCycle()` (fail-open: any read error ⇒ true).
- Gate the scheduler tasks in `runWorklistTui`:
  - `refresh` tick: skip (spawn nothing) when the DB is unchanged since the last cycle.
  - `sync` tick: skip `wl sync` when DB unchanged **and** last successful sync (heartbeat marker) is within the configurable max-staleness cap; otherwise run `doSync` + `doRefresh` as today.
  - `resume-poll` hidden→visible transition: apply the same DB-change gate (list content is identical when nothing changed).
  - Manual `S`/`r` paths unchanged (always run).
- Add the configurable cap to settings (e.g. `maxSyncStalenessMs`, default 60s, clamped ≥1s or aligned with the sync-interval clamp) and pass it through `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Keep all existing guards (heartbeat, single-flight, `--if-idle`) for syncs that do run.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — NEW: pure DB-change signal reader (wl cache-dir resolution + state-counter read + last-seen tracker), fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — expose/adapt staleness helpers (reuse `readSyncHeartbeatMs`) so the sync tick can decide "DB unchanged AND sync fresh ⇒ skip".
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — wire the gate into the `refresh` / `sync` / `resume-poll` scheduler tasks; manual `S`/`r` untouched.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting (default `60000`) with clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the new setting into `runWorklistTui`.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — read-only reference for the counter-file format/path derivation (no changes expected).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (NEW), plus updates to `auto-sync.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W` — Cross-instance sync heartbeat (F3): the `last-sync-time` marker and heartbeat TTL this change composes with. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` — wl sync lock storm: auto-sync single-flight / `--if-idle` guards; gating reduces spawn pressure further. Completed.
- `WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA` — wl CLI read cache (F2) with the state-counter fingerprint this gate reuses as its signal. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q` — Incremental sync: only export/push changed work items (CLI-side; explicitly out of scope here). Open.
- `WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B` — Smart-selection duplication decision (Q2c): precedent for duplicating a small pure helper into the Herdr package. Completed.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — release workflow (no code impact; doc reference).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Remote-pull latency (accepted tradeoff, user-confirmed):** skipping `wl sync` when the DB is unchanged delays pulling remote changes until the next sync that does run. Bounded by the max-staleness cap (default 60s) so remote freshness is never worse than the cap.
- **Signal completeness:** the state counter is bumped by wl CLI writes and post-sync invalidation. External tools writing the SQLite DB directly (not via wl) would not bump it — mitigated by the staleness cap, which forces a periodic sync regardless. Assumed acceptable.
- **Configurable cap naming/units:** `maxSyncStalenessMs` in ms, default 60000, clamped to ≥1s (aligned with `heartbeatTtlForInterval`'s clamp) — exact name subject to implementer/plan review.
- **Scope-creep guard:** incremental sync (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q), event-driven window subscription (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ), and WAL checkpointing (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) are tracked separately and must NOT be pulled into this work item.
- **Behavioral parity:** when the DB IS changing, cadence must match today (no additional latency); only the no-change case adds skipping.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked 2026-08-07): "If the local DB hasn't changed, should the background `wl sync` also be skipped? That means remote changes pushed by other machines would only be pulled when local activity bumps the counter (or via manual `S`). Acceptable — or should the sync path stay ungated while only the refresh reads are skipped?" — Answer (user): "Partially acceptable. wl sync can be skipped if no local DB changes. However, it should not go more than 1 minute (configurable) without being run." Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC2/AC3: sync is gated by (DB unchanged AND last successful sync within configurable max-staleness cap, default 60s).
- Q2 (asked 2026-08-07): "Should manual refresh (`r`) and manual sync (`S`) always run regardless of the check? (My assumption: yes — user-initiated actions always execute.)" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC4.
- Q3 (asked 2026-08-07, /skill:find-related): "Which work items are related?" — Research: the find-related script (`find_related.py --work-item-id WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ`) resolved the wrong worklog store (SorraAgents framework repo) on both runs and returned unrelated items (OpenBrain submission, file-path convention, a-y shortcut). The matches were excluded per the skill's conservative policy (false negatives preferred); the curated Related work section above (verified via `wl show` against the ContextHub store) is authoritative.
data.title: Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)

## Headline

Flip the space priority in the Herdr worklist pane: the selection list may use up to the full available pane height (including its header lines), and the metadata section fills whatever space remains — expanding when the list is short, sitting below the fold (revealed by scrolling down) when the list is long — scrolling internally when its content overflows.

## Problem statement

The metadata section below the selection list currently reserves a fixed 20–40% of the pane height (`computeMetadataPanelHeight`), squeezing the list. When the list needs more vertical space than it is allotted, it scrolls and the header/top lines scroll off the top of the pane, even though the metadata section below is eating rows the list could use. The metadata section should no longer force the list to scroll off the top.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selection list — including its header line — to use as much vertical space as it needs, up to the maximum available, so items don't scroll off the top prematurely.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when the list is long, I want the list (header + items) to take up to the full pane height so I can see as many items as possible without the top scrolling off.
- As a Herdr user, when the list is short, I want the metadata section to expand into the leftover space so the pane still shows the selected item's metadata.
- As a Herdr user, when the list fills the full pane, I want to scroll the pane down to expose the rest of the list and then the metadata section, with the initial view starting at the top of the selection list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List takes as much space as it needs, up to the max available**: The selection list (header line + items + group separators + footer) can use up to the maximum number of vertical lines available in the pane (pane rows minus the reserved notification row). The metadata section no longer reserves a fixed 20–40% share that forces the list to scroll.
2. **Initial view at top**: When the list fills the full vertical space, the view starts at the top of the selection list (header + first items visible). Scrolling the pane down exposes the rest of the list and, at the end, the metadata section.
3. **Metadata fills the rest**: When the list content is shorter than the available height, the metadata section expands to fill the leftover space below the list.
4. **Metadata scrolls if necessary**: When the metadata content overflows the space allotted to it, it scrolls independently using the existing `m`/`M` keys and `metaScrollOffset` (with the existing `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator), and the selection-driven reset behaviour is preserved.
5. **No regression**: Keyboard navigation (arrows/j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap), stage filtering, group separators, auto-refresh, code-freeze banner, and the reserved notification row continue to work; rendered output never exceeds the pane's `rows` budget.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests cover (a) list height = min(content need, max available), (b) metadata expansion when the list is short, (c) reveal-by-scroll when the list fills the pane and initial view at top, (d) metadata scroll clamping under the new layout, and (e) the output line-count invariant (≤ `rows`).
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Plugin-local change in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; no `wl` CLI or backend schema changes.
- The rendered output must never exceed the pane's `rows` budget (last row reserved for the notification line; group-separator accounting must not overflow) — the invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO must hold.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings: `m`/`M` for metadata scrolling, and all list-navigation keys unchanged.
- Must compose with the description preview feature (WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3, in progress) which adds up to 3 preview lines to the metadata panel content.
- The metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) whenever it is rendered (short list or scrolled into view) so it remains usable, even if that means its content scrolls internally.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — document-flow layout**: the user's answers describe the list and metadata section as stacked content within one scrollable viewport (view starts at top; scrolling down reveals the rest of the list, then the metadata). An alternative pinned-footer layout (metadata always visible at the pane bottom) does not match the answers and is out of scope.
- **Assumption — header behavior**: "start the view at the top of the selection list" is interpreted as the initial render showing header + first items; the exact pin-vs-scroll behaviour of the header line during scroll is an implementation detail, but the header must be visible initially (matching the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO invariant that the header is never cut off).
- **Risk — line-count regression**: changing the list/metadata space split could reintroduce output overflowing the pane (the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO bug). Mitigation: keep the ≤ `rows` invariant as an explicit test.
- **Risk — metadata scroll clamping**: if the panel's allotted height changes dynamically, `metaScrollDown`'s clamp against content height must still hold; keep the existing clamp tests and update them for the new sizing.
- **Risk — scope creep**: "below the fold" indicators (WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ), mouse/touch scrolling (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ), and metadata panel content changes (WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7) are related but separate items — do not implement them here.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)` (lines ~85–119) — reserves a 20–40% share of pane rows for the metadata panel (min 3 rows), from WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X.
  - `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` (line ~681) — `max(3, rows - 4 - panelHeight)`; used by `_adjustScroll` and `getVisibleItems`.
  - `createListRenderer()` (line ~1830) — computes `panelHeight = computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)`, `listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`, `listHeight = rows - 4 - panelHeight`; renders header + items + separators + fill + footer + metadata panel lines, clamped to `rows - 1`.
  - `formatMetadataPanel()` (line ~982) — renders exactly `panelRows` lines with independent scroll offset and `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator; `metaScrollDown` clamps against content height.
  - `metaScrollOffset` reset on selection change (`_resetMetaScroll`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `computeMetadataPanelHeight` responsive-ramp tests (lines ~1448), metadata scroll clamp tests (line ~1663), renderer line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point wiring (render callback passes `metaScrollOffset`/`metaLastCommand`).

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer()`: compute the list's space need from its content (header + banner + items + separators + footer), capped at the maximum available rows (`rows - 1` minus the notification budget). The metadata section is allotted the remainder: it expands to fill leftover space when the list is short, and when the list fills the pane it is positioned below the list content so scrolling down reveals the rest of the list and then the metadata section.
- Initial view starts at the top of the selection list (scroll offset 0 / header visible) even when the list is long.
- Keep `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (or replace its call sites) such that the fixed 20–40% reservation no longer forces the list to scroll; the metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) and scrolls internally via `metaScrollOffset`/`m`/`M` when its content overflows.
- Keep `formatMetadataPanel`'s independent-scroll contract (exactly `panelRows` lines) and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list/metadata space split, initial view-at-top, metadata scroll clamping; primary change location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — update responsive-ramp tests; add list-height/content-need, metadata-expansion, reveal-by-scroll, and line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — render callback wiring (`metaScrollOffset`, `metaLastCommand`), only if the space split needs state/context passed through.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** (completed) — introduced the metadata panel and the fixed 20–40% reservation this item reverses; its AC1 said the list "always keeps the majority of the space (≥60%)" — this item changes that priority.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** (in progress) — adds a description preview to the metadata panel (up to 3 lines), which makes the metadata content taller; this item must compose with it.
- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** (completed) — the output line-count invariant (`≤ rows`) this item must preserve.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** (open) — "no indication of items below the fold" — related scrolling UX; not required by this item but related.
- **WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7** (open) — drops the duplicate ID row from the metadata panel; touches the same `formatMetadataPanel` output.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When the list is long and fills the pane, should the metadata panel keep a small guaranteed minimum (e.g., ~3 rows, as today) so it stays visible and scrolls within that, or may it shrink all the way to zero (hidden)?" — Answer (user): "If the selection list takes up the full vertical space scrolling the pane down should expose the rest of the list and the meta-data section. However we should start the view at the top of the selection list." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: when the list fills the pane, the metadata section sits below the list content and is revealed by scrolling the pane down; the initial view starts at the top of the selection list (header visible). Research: inspected `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (20–40% fixed reservation) and the renderer's `listArea`/`listHeight` budget in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q2: "When the list has only a few items, should the list take only the rows it needs (header + items + separators + footer) and let the metadata panel expand to fill the leftover space, or should the list always occupy the full available height and the metadata panel stay at a fixed small size?" — Answer (user): "meta-data can expand to fill space." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the list takes only what it needs when short; the metadata section expands into the leftover space.
- Q3: "Should the existing m/M metadata scrolling behavior stay as-is, just operating in the new (possibly smaller) panel space?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Research: `metaScrollOffset`, `_resetMetaScroll` on selection change, `metaScrollUp/Down` clamping and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator already exist in `worklist.ts`.
data.title: Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls

Sync-clobber bug reverts soft-deletes (known in WL-0MSPZP7FE009YXPG), and `wl doctor prune` has never been run (778 soft-deleted items accumulate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2**: `tests/e2e/agent-flow.test.ts` has teardown that deletes created items

## Implementation Notes

2. Same for agent-flow test

## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo
data.title: wl doctor prune cannot persist: sync re-adds pruned items from remote ref

As an operator, I do not want the herdr downtime worker to inhibit dispatch based on the GLOBAL active_query signal when the proxy serves the local-only signal, so that remote/cloud streams never block local downtime dispatch. The backward-compatibility fallback to the global `active_query` for pre-fix proxies must be removed.

## Background

- `isIdleStatus`/`globalIdleChecks` in packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts: `const queryActive = status.local_active_query !== undefined ? status.local_active_query : status.active_query;` — the fallback to `active_query` exists for proxies that predate the `local_active_queries` counter (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR, delivered in WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q).
- The global `active_query` is true whenever ANY request is in flight — local AND remote provider streams. Remote streams keep it true while the local model is idle with free slots, so the fallback can block legitimate downtime dispatch (RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7).
- The local-only signal (`local_active_query`) is the correct busy signal for the local model.

## Design notes

- Remove the `local_active_query !== undefined ? ... : active_query` fallback; use only `local_active_query`.
- Fail-closed question to resolve: is a MISSING `local_active_query` now treated as busy (no dispatch) or idle (dispatch)? Decision: treat a missing signal as busy (fail-closed, consistent with the rest of the worker) — a pre-fix proxy must not cause dispatch on an unverifiable signal.
- parseLlamaStatus currently accepts an absent `local_active_query` (`undefined`); a work item must decide whether absence becomes null (busy) or a documented explicit non-dispatch.
- Update parseLlamaStatus doc + isIdleStatus/globalIdleChecks comments (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR reference).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `globalIdleChecks` uses ONLY `local_active_query` once present in the payload; the `active_query` fallback is removed.
2. A payload WITHOUT `local_active_query` fails closed: the worker treats the status as busy (no dispatch) and the behaviour is documented — no silent degraded dispatch on pre-fix proxies.
3. Remote/cloud streams (global active_query true, local false) are never a dispatch inhibitor.
4. Test suite covers: local_active_query present (both values), local_active_query absent (busy), and the removal of the fallback branch.
data.title: Downtime idle detection: remove fallback to global active_query when local_active_query absent (fail-closed busy)

# Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

## Problem statement

During downtime dispatching through the leader, only a single audit should ever be active at any one time. The dispatch logic must check for existing active audits (dispatched but not yet completed) and skip dispatching another audit if one is already in progress, ensuring audits are strictly sequential rather than allowing fan-out.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants audit work to progress deterministically, one at a time, without competing audits consuming LLM capacity.
- **Operator relying on audit results for release decisions** — needs audit outcomes to be reliable and complete; concurrent audits increase the risk of missed findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Leader-only check** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; non-leader instances do not dispatch audits at all (unchanged behavior).
3. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for any audit-tier item (completed/in_review candidates) that has a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `audit`. If the dispatched audit entry is older than a stale threshold (2 hours), it is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier. The skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability.
5. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Audit tier only** — this constraint applies only to the audit dispatch tier; implement/plan/intake tiers are unaffected.
- **Existing single-flight guard** — the in-process `dispatchInFlight` guard remains in place; this adds a cross-idle-period guard (prevents re-dispatch on the next idle tick while a previous audit is still running).
- **Coordination file aware** — in the leader-election refactor context, the check must consider audits dispatched by any instance (not just the current instance), using the coordination file or dispatch log as the source of truth.
- **Fail-safe** — if the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the dispatcher falls through to the next tier rather than blocking all dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` dispatches audit-tier items via `dispatchClaimedTier(deps, 'audit', ...)`.
- The `dispatchInFlight` guard prevents concurrent dispatch calls within the same idle period.
- CAS claim moves dispatched items to `in_progress`, removing them from `wl next`/`wl list` selection.
- Dispatched markers in `downtime-dispatches.log` track dispatched items with kind and timestamp.
- The audit tier runs first, before implement/plan/intake tiers.
- Under the leader-election refactor (WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), only the leader dispatches, but multiple idle periods could span across a running audit.

## Desired change

1. **Active audit check** — Before selecting an audit candidate, query whether any audit-tier item is currently active (dispatched and `in_progress`). This can be done by: (a) scanning the dispatched-marker log for recent audit dispatches where the item is still `in_progress`, or (b) querying the worklog for `in_progress` items that match audit-tier criteria.
2. **Audit tier skip** — If an active audit is found, skip the audit tier and proceed to the implement tier (unchanged fallback behavior).
3. **Logging** — Log the skip reason (`audit-in-flight`) for observability.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork`: add active-audit check before `getNextAuditCandidate`; skip audit tier if active audit found; log skip reason.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — possibly a new dep method `getActiveAudits(cwd)` or reuse existing dispatched-marker logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests: audit skipped when one active, audit dispatched when none active, active-audit check failure falls through gracefully.

## Related work

- **WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL** — Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file (open, plan_complete) — the primary context; this constraint applies to the leader-only dispatch model.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed) — establishes the audit tier.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed) — parent for dispatched-marker exclusion.

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (open) — directly relevant to stale-audit timeout design; a crashed audit pane that fails to update the work item state is the scenario the timeout protects against.
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed) — proxy idle/busy semantics relevant to dispatch timing.
- **WL-0ML7QRBQR183KXPB** — Auto-unblock on dependency changes (completed) — dependency resolution patterns may inform how active-audit detection handles blocked items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** An audit is considered "active" from the moment it is dispatched (marked in `downtime-dispatches.log`) until the item transitions from `in_progress` to a terminal state (`completed`/`in_review` with a fresh audit, or reverted to `completed/in_review` for re-audit).
- **Assumption:** The dispatch log or worklog query is fast enough to not impact dispatch latency (should be sub-second for typical worklog sizes).

- **Risk:** The active-audit check adds complexity to the dispatch loop. Mitigation: keep the check simple (one worklog query or log scan) and fail-open (skip audit tier on query failure).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Extending this constraint to implement/plan/intake tiers is out of scope. Only audit-tier sequentialization is required.
- **Risk (leader-election context):** Multiple instances could have stale active-audit entries from crashed instances. Mitigation: the check should use the coordination file or dispatch log timestamps to detect stale entries.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the single-audit constraint apply only to audits, or to all dispatch tiers?" — Answer (user): "Audit only. Implement/plan/intake are not affected." Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "How should we detect an 'active' audit? By worklog status or dispatch log?" — Answer (user): "Check for audit-tier items that are dispatched but not yet completed — use the dispatched markers or worklog query. The check must work in the leader-election context." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "What happens if the active-audit check fails?" — Answer (user): "Fail-open: skip the audit tier and fall through to implement. Do not block all dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Should there be a timeout on active audits? (e.g., if an audit pane crashes, the item stays in_progress forever)" — Answer (user): "Yes — add a stale-audit timeout. If an audit dispatch entry is older than a reasonable threshold (e.g., 2 hours), treat it as stale and allow re-dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

# Active-audit single-flight tests

## Summary

Test battery pinning the single-active-audit guarantee in the downtime dispatcher before implementation: audits dispatch when none is active, are skipped (falling through to the implement tier) when one is active, treat stale dispatch markers as expired, and fail open when the active-audit check itself fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit dispatched when none active** — When no audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (no non-stale `kind=audit` dispatch entry maps to an `in_progress` item), the audit tier dispatches as today.
2. **One active audit → audit tier skipped** — When an audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed), the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier (implement).
3. **Stale dispatch entry ignored** — An audit dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with `kind` `audit` older than the stale threshold (2 hours) is treated as stale and ignored; a new audit dispatch proceeds.
4. **Active-audit-check failure fails open** — When the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to implement without blocking all dispatch.
5. **Audit-in-flight reason logged** — An audit-in-flight skip with an empty implement/plan/intake backlog reports outcome reason `audit-in-flight` (never `no-candidate`), so the no-candidate cooldown is not entered (mirrors the `code-freeze` precedent); skip logged for observability.
6. **Existing guards unchanged** — Regression tests for the single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate pass unchanged.
7. **Full project test suite passes** — The complete test suite passes with the new tests.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `describe` blocks to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` covering scenarios 1–5 above.
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` for marker-age/stale-window helper coverage.
- Fixtures: dispatched-log entries (`kind=audit`, `dispatchedAt` ages: fresh / stale / unrelated-kind); mock worklog `in_progress` queries (empty, matching, failing).
- Assert outcome reasons (`audit` dispatched vs `audit-in-flight` skip vs `no-candidate` absence) and tier fall-through.

# Active-audit detection & audit-tier skip

## Summary

Add an active-audit detection dependency (`getActiveAudit(cwd)`) that reads `kind=audit` dispatch markers from `downtime-dispatches.log` within a 2-hour stale window and confirms the item is still `in_progress` via a single worklog query; gate the audit tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` and log the skip reason `audit-in-flight`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for audit-tier items that have a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with `kind` `audit`; a dispatched audit entry older than a stale threshold (2 hours) is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
3. **Stale window constant** — A named constant `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_STALE_WINDOW_MS` (= 2 hours) defines the stale threshold; entries older than it are ignored.
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier; the skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability, and when the remaining backlog is empty the outcome is `audit-in-flight` (never `no-candidate`), so the no-candidate cooldown is not entered (mirrors `code-freeze`).
5. **Fail-open on check failure** — If the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier; dispatch is never blocked.
6. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
7. **Leader-only check scope** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; the check is placed in the audit-tier dispatch path only (leader-only under WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), with no new instance-local state, so non-leader instances do not dispatch audits (unchanged behavior).
8. **Full project test suite passes** — The complete test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `DowntimeWorkerDeps` with `getActiveAudit(cwd)` (returns `{ ok, active }`-shaped result).
- Implement in `createDowntimeDeps` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) using `readDowntimeLogEntries` + one `wl list --status in_progress --json` query intersected with non-stale audit dispatched ids; fail-open (never throws).
- Wire the gate into `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) immediately before `getNextAuditCandidate`, within the audit tier branch; add the `audit-in-flight` outcome reason + stderr/log observability.
- Add `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_STALE_WINDOW_MS` constant (2h).
- Verify against F1 test battery; run full suite.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (Active-audit single-flight tests) — test-first prerequisite.

## Deliverables

Production code changes + passing full test suite.
